title: Titration Simulation with pH Indicator & Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D acid-base titration simulation using Three.js (CDN). The scene simulates adding NaOH (strong base) from a burette into an Erlenmeyer flask containing HCl (strong acid) with a phenolphthalein indicator, complete with particle effects.

## Scene Setup
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 8, 14), looking at origin.
- Lights: Ambient light (0x404040, intensity 0.6) + directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.9) from (5, 10, 7).
- Background: gradient dark lab background color 0x1a1a2e.
- Floor: A flat plane (20x20) with a dark grey lab-bench material at y=0.
- Burette: A tall thin cylinder (radius 0.15, height 6) positioned at (0, 7, 0), semi-transparent glass material (opacity 0.3, color 0xaaddff). Inside, a smaller cylinder represents the NaOH liquid level (color 0x4488ff), whose height decreases as titrant is dispensed.
- Erlenmeyer Flask: Approximate with a truncated cone (radiusTop=0.8, radiusBottom=1.5, height=3) at (0, 1.5, 0), semi-transparent glass (opacity 0.25). Inside, a liquid mesh whose color changes with pH.
- Stopcock: A small box (0.3x0.15x0.15) on the burette at y=3.5, colored red when closed, green when open.
- Magnetic stirrer: A small rotating bar at the bottom of the flask interior.

## Chemistry Model
- Initial state: Flask contains 50 mL of 0.1 M HCl (strong acid). Burette contains 50 mL of 0.1 M NaOH.
- Each drop is 0.5 mL of NaOH. pH is calculated using strong acid-strong base titration formula:
  - Before equivalence: pH = -log10([H+] remaining)
  - At equivalence (25 mL added): pH = 7.0
  - After equivalence: pOH = -log10([OH-] excess), pH = 14 - pOH
- Phenolphthalein indicator: liquid is colorless (0xf0f0f0) below pH 8.2, transitions through pink (0xff69b4) between 8.2-10.0, and deep magenta (0xcc0066) above 10.0. Interpolate color smoothly.
- Track: volumeAdded, pH, molesHCl remaining, molesNaOH added, totalVolume.

## Particle Effects
- When the stopcock is open and drops fall, spawn 3D particle drops (small spheres, radius 0.05, color 0x4488ff) that fall from the burette tip to the flask opening with gravity (acceleration 9.8 units/s²).
- On splash into the flask liquid, spawn 8-12 tiny splash particles that spread outward and fade (reduce opacity over 0.5s then remove).
- When pH crosses 7.0 (equivalence point), trigger a burst of 30 golden sparkle particles (0xffd700) that rise upward from the flask and fade.
- Stirrer particles: 6 small white particles orbiting inside the flask liquid to show mixing.

## User Interactions
- SPACEBAR: Toggle stopcock open/closed. When open, drops fall at a rate of 1 drop per 0.8 seconds.
- UP/DOWN Arrow keys: Adjust drop rate (0.3s to 2.0s per drop, step 0.1s). Only works when stopcock is open.
- 'R' key: Reset entire simulation to initial state.
- 'S' key: Toggle magnetic stirrer on/off (stirrer rotates when on).
- Mouse click on flask: Show a floating DOM tooltip with current pH, volume added, and indicator status.
- DOM Button 'Add Single Drop': Adds exactly one drop regardless of stopcock state.
- DOM Button 'Auto-Titrate to Equivalence': Automatically adds drops until equivalence point is reached (25 mL), then stops.

## HUD / DOM UI
- Top-left panel (semi-transparent dark background):
  - pH value (2 decimal places)
  - Volume NaOH added (1 decimal place) in mL
  - Drop rate (current interval)
  - Stopcock status (OPEN/CLOSED)
  - Stirrer status (ON/OFF)
  - Indicator color name (Colorless / Transition / Pink)
- Two buttons below the panel: 'Add Single Drop' (id='btn-single-drop') and 'Auto-Titrate' (id='btn-auto-titrate').
- A pH strip bar on the right side of the screen: a vertical gradient bar (0-14) with a marker showing current pH.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- pH: number (2 decimal precision)
- volumeAdded: number (mL, 1 decimal precision)
- totalVolume: number (mL, initial liquid + added)
- molesHClRemaining: number
- molesNaOHAdded: number
- stopcockOpen: boolean
- stirrerOn: boolean
- dropRate: number (seconds per drop)
- dropCount: integer (total drops dispensed)
- activeParticles: integer (current live particle count)
- equivalenceReached: boolean
- indicatorState: string ('colorless'|'transition'|'pink')
- liquidColorHex: string (hex color of flask liquid)
- buretteLevel: number (mL remaining in burette, starts at 50)
- splashParticlesTotal: integer (cumulative splash particles spawned)
- equivalenceBurstFired: boolean
- resetCount: integer (how many times reset was triggered)
- autoTitrating: boolean
- lastDropTime: number (timestamp of last drop)

## Conservation Law
- At all times: molesHClRemaining + molesNaOHAdded must relate correctly. Total moles of acid initially = 0.005 (50mL * 0.1M). molesNaOHAdded = dropCount * 0.5mL * 0.1M = dropCount * 0.00005. molesHClRemaining = max(0, 0.005 - molesNaOHAdded).
- buretteLevel = 50 - volumeAdded. Must never go negative.
- volumeAdded = dropCount * 0.5. Must be consistent.

Ensure all values are NaN-free and physically consistent at all times.
physics_constraints: Strong acid-strong base titration: pH = -log10([H+]) before equivalence, pH=7 at equivalence (25mL NaOH into 50mL 0.1M HCl), pH = 14+log10([OH-]) after equivalence. Conservation: initial moles HCl = 0.005. molesNaOH added = dropCount * 0.00005. Particle gravity = 9.8 units/s². buretteLevel + volumeAdded = 50 always. totalVolume = 50 + volumeAdded.
